newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle coin sales rise in December - CPM.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle coin sales rise in December - CPM.

text.p: Lower gold and silver prices, coupled with holiday gift buying, led to a healthy increase in sales of American Eagle gold and silver coins throughout the month of December 1996, CPM Group said.
"Traditionally, the holiday season alone tends to cause a marked increase in the gold and silver Eagle purchases," said CPM Group managing director Jeffrey Christian.
For December, American Eagle gold coin sales were 71,000 ounces, up more than threefold from November's 22,000 ounces. Year-on-year, sales rose 26.8 percent from 56,000 ounces in December 1995.
Similarly, sales of American Eagle silver coins rose almost three fold to 1.34 million ounces in December from 450,000 ounces in November.
Year-on-year though, silver coin sales were 28.4 percent lower in the final month of 1996 from 1.88 million ounces in 1995.
The U.S. Mint hopes to launch proof platinum Eagles perhaps as early as March, with the uncirculated bullion platinum Eagles being released in the summer, CPM Group said.
